classification.difficultyReason: Checks two bearings-triangle configurations and uses the nearer-mountain condition to select the required bearing.

inlines.text: From an observatory tower, a scout can see a mountain at a bearing of 140° and a waterfall at a bearing of 160°.

It is known that the waterfall is 35 km from the mountain, and the waterfall is 60 km away from the observatory tower. The scout can also see that the mountain is closer to the tower than the waterfall.
Find the bearing of the mountain from the waterfall, correct to the nearest degree.

answer.short:
$356^\circ$.

Check both sine-rule triangles and retain the one in which the mountain is closer to the tower than the waterfall.
answer.worked:
Let $T$, $M$ and $W$ denote the tower, mountain and waterfall.
$$\begin{align*}\angle MTW&=160^\circ-140^\circ\\\angle MTW&=20^\circ\\\frac{\sin\angle TMW}{60}&=\frac{\sin20^\circ}{35}\\\sin\angle TMW&=\frac{60\sin20^\circ}{35}\end{align*}$$
Let $\alpha=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{60\sin20^\circ}{35}\right)$. The possible angles at $M$ are $\alpha$ and $180^\circ-\alpha$.

For $\angle TMW=\alpha$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle TWM&=180^\circ-20^\circ-\alpha\\\angle TWM&=160^\circ-\alpha\\TM&=\frac{35\sin(160^\circ-\alpha)}{\sin20^\circ}\\TM&\approx84.73\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
This is greater than $TW=60\text{ km}$, so it contradicts the nearer-mountain condition.

For $\angle TMW=180^\circ-\alpha$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle TWM&=180^\circ-20^\circ-(180^\circ-\alpha)\\\angle TWM&=\alpha-20^\circ\\TM&=\frac{35\sin(\alpha-20^\circ)}{\sin20^\circ}\\TM&\approx28.03\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
This satisfies $TM<60\text{ km}$. The bearing of $T$ from $W$ is $340^\circ$, and $M$ lies clockwise from this direction. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\text{bearing of }M\text{ from }W&=340^\circ+(\alpha-20^\circ)\\\text{bearing of }M\text{ from }W&=320^\circ+\alpha\\\text{bearing of }M\text{ from }W&\approx355.8963^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The bearing is $356^\circ$, to the nearest degree.
